Daytime handler pairs rules
This page teaches how a new handler works
This topic matters because the desk keeps each journey orderly from booking through pickup, and every note you enter supports the animal, the passenger, and the cabin team. You begin by reading the file carefully, checking the travel request, the animal details, and any service notes already attached to the booking. Keep your tone calm and precise, since many passengers arrive with concern and need clear guidance from the first contact.

As a new handler, you work beside the senior coordinator and follow the daily service plan without delay. Record each update in plain language and keep the file current after every conversation. If a passenger reports a change in kennel size, feeding needs, or transfer plans, note it at once and pass it to the proper desk member. The cabin team depends on accurate records, so do not leave uncertainty in the file. When a passenger is worried, listen carefully, answer in a steady manner, and confirm the next step before ending the exchange. If the matter calls for review, bring it to the senior coordinator rather than guessing.

Use the same careful method at the counter, on the phone, and in written notes. Check that tags, carrier details, and contact information match the booking. Keep attention on the animal's comfort and on the passenger's understanding of the process. If a handoff is due, prepare the record so the receiving staff can act without confusion. Should a pet arrive with a special instruction, place that note where it can be found quickly and follow the approved service path. Regular desk work is simple only when every record is complete and every transfer is clear.

Remember to work steadily, record accurately, and seek guidance whenever a note is unclear.
